front_blocks.md: Define **population growth rate**.

back_blocks.md: The **average annual change** in the size of a population over a set period, usually a year.

cards.front_md: Define **population growth rate**.
cards.back_md: The **average annual change** in the size of a population over a set period, usually a year.

front_blocks.md: What was the world's population growth rate in 1970 compared with 2022?

back_blocks.md: In **1970** the growth rate was **2%**; by **2022** it had fallen to **under 1%**.

cards.front_md: What was the world's population growth rate in 1970 compared with 2022?
cards.back_md: In **1970** the growth rate was **2%**; by **2022** it had fallen to **under 1%**.

front_blocks.md: After 1804, it took just over ______ years for the world population to double to 2 billion.

back_blocks.md: After 1804, it took just over **100** years for the world population to double to 2 billion.

cards.front_md: After 1804, it took just over ______ years for the world population to double to 2 billion.
cards.back_md: After 1804, it took just over **100** years for the world population to double to 2 billion.

front_blocks.md: What factors have driven the rapid global increase in population?

back_blocks.md: Improvements in **agriculture**, **medicine**, **technology**, and **clean water supply and sanitation**, which lowered the **death rate**.

cards.front_md: What factors have driven the rapid global increase in population?
cards.back_md: Improvements in **agriculture**, **medicine**, **technology**, and **clean water supply and sanitation**, which lowered the **death rate**.

front_blocks.md: The fastest increase in world population happened during the ______ and ______.

back_blocks.md: The fastest increase in world population happened during the** 1980s **and **1990s**.

cards.front_md: The fastest increase in world population happened during the ______ and ______.
cards.back_md: The fastest increase in world population happened during the** 1980s **and **1990s**.

front_blocks.md: Define **net migration**.

back_blocks.md: The **difference** between the number of people **moving into** a country (immigrants) and the number **leaving** it (emigrants).

cards.front_md: Define **net migration**.
cards.back_md: The **difference** between the number of people **moving into** a country (immigrants) and the number **leaving** it (emigrants).

front_blocks.md: Natural change in population is calculated by subtracting the ______ rate from the ______ rate.

back_blocks.md: Natural change in population is calculated by subtracting the **death** rate from the **birth** rate.

cards.front_md: Natural change in population is calculated by subtracting the ______ rate from the ______ rate.
cards.back_md: Natural change in population is calculated by subtracting the **death** rate from the **birth** rate.

front_blocks.md: How is the **birth rate** calculated?

back_blocks.md: **Total births ÷ total population × 1000** — the number of **live births per 1000 people** per year.

cards.front_md: How is the **birth rate** calculated?
cards.back_md: **Total births ÷ total population × 1000** — the number of **live births per 1000 people** per year.

front_blocks.md: Define **fertility rate**.

back_blocks.md: The number of **live births per 1000 women aged 15–49** in a given year.

cards.front_md: Define **fertility rate**.
cards.back_md: The number of **live births per 1000 women aged 15–49** in a given year.

front_blocks.md: What happens when the birth rate is lower than the death rate?

back_blocks.md: A **negative natural increase** occurs, so the **population declines**.

cards.front_md: What happens when the birth rate is lower than the death rate?
cards.back_md: A **negative natural increase** occurs, so the **population declines**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Natural change is the birth rate minus the death rate.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Natural change** is the **birth rate minus the death rate**. When the death rate is higher, a **negative natural increase** occurs and the population declines.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Natural change is the birth rate minus the death rate.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

**Natural change** is the **birth rate minus the death rate**. When the death rate is higher, a **negative natural increase** occurs and the population declines.

front_blocks.md: Define a **pro-natalist policy**.

back_blocks.md: A government policy designed to **encourage** people to have more children and **increase the birth rate**.

cards.front_md: Define a **pro-natalist policy**.
cards.back_md: A government policy designed to **encourage** people to have more children and **increase the birth rate**.

front_blocks.md: Name two measures used by France to encourage larger families.

back_blocks.md: Discounts on public transport for families with three or more children, and increased paid maternity leave.

cards.front_md: Name two measures used by France to encourage larger families.
cards.back_md: Discounts on public transport for families with three or more children, and increased paid maternity leave.

front_blocks.md: A country that introduced a baby bonus to encourage larger families is ________.

back_blocks.md: A country that introduced a baby bonus to encourage larger families is Singapore.

cards.front_md: A country that introduced a baby bonus to encourage larger families is ________.
cards.back_md: A country that introduced a baby bonus to encourage larger families is Singapore.

front_blocks.md: Why do some countries adopt pro-natalist policies?

back_blocks.md: To address issues such as an ageing population, workforce shortages, and reduced tax payments due to fewer workers.

cards.front_md: Why do some countries adopt pro-natalist policies?
cards.back_md: To address issues such as an ageing population, workforce shortages, and reduced tax payments due to fewer workers.

front_blocks.md: Define an **anti-natalist policy**.

back_blocks.md: A government policy aimed at **reducing the birth rate** to slow population growth and ease pressure on **resources**.

cards.front_md: Define an **anti-natalist policy**.
cards.back_md: A government policy aimed at **reducing the birth rate** to slow population growth and ease pressure on **resources**.

front_blocks.md: What was the main goal of China's one-child policy?

back_blocks.md: To reduce the birth rate and slow down the rapid population growth.

cards.front_md: What was the main goal of China's one-child policy?
cards.back_md: To reduce the birth rate and slow down the rapid population growth.

front_blocks.md: China's one-child policy was in effect from 1979 to ________.

back_blocks.md: China's one-child policy was in effect from 1979 to 2016.

cards.front_md: China's one-child policy was in effect from 1979 to ________.
cards.back_md: China's one-child policy was in effect from 1979 to 2016.

front_blocks.md: List two negative impacts of China's one-child policy.

back_blocks.md: It led to a male/female imbalance and an ageing population.

cards.front_md: List two negative impacts of China's one-child policy.
cards.back_md: It led to a male/female imbalance and an ageing population.

front_blocks.md: Define **family planning education**.

back_blocks.md: Teaching people about **contraception** and how to control the number and timing of children, in order to **reduce the birth rate**.

cards.front_md: Define **family planning education**.
cards.back_md: Teaching people about **contraception** and how to control the number and timing of children, in order to **reduce the birth rate**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
China's one-child policy led to more men than women in the younger population.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A preference for male children skewed the **male/female ratio**, leaving over **30 million more men than women under 20**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

China's one-child policy led to more men than women in the younger population.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

A preference for male children skewed the **male/female ratio**, leaving over **30 million more men than women under 20**.

front_blocks.md: Define the **demographic transition model (DTM)**.

back_blocks.md: The **DTM** shows the five generalised stages of population change that countries pass through as they develop, tracking how **birth** and **death rates** change over time.

cards.front_md: Define the **demographic transition model (DTM)**.
cards.back_md: The **DTM** shows the five generalised stages of population change that countries pass through as they develop, tracking how **birth** and **death rates** change over time.

front_blocks.md: The demographic transition model has **______** generalised stages of population change.

back_blocks.md: The demographic transition model has **five** generalised stages of population change.

cards.front_md: The demographic transition model has **______** generalised stages of population change.
cards.back_md: The demographic transition model has **five** generalised stages of population change.

front_blocks.md: Describe the birth rate, death rate and population in **Stage 1** of the DTM.

back_blocks.md: **High birth rate** and **high death rate**, giving a **low** total population.

cards.front_md: Describe the birth rate, death rate and population in **Stage 1** of the DTM.
cards.back_md: **High birth rate** and **high death rate**, giving a **low** total population.

front_blocks.md: Why do death rates fall in **Stage 2** of the DTM?

back_blocks.md: Because of **improved diets**, **better healthcare**, **lower infant mortality** and increased access to **clean water**; birth rates stay high, so population rises rapidly.

cards.front_md: Why do death rates fall in **Stage 2** of the DTM?
cards.back_md: Because of **improved diets**, **better healthcare**, **lower infant mortality** and increased access to **clean water**; birth rates stay high, so population rises rapidly.

front_blocks.md: In **Stage 3** of the DTM, what happens to the birth rate and why?

back_blocks.md: The birth rate **falls rapidly** due to increased **birth control** and family planning, the rising **cost of raising children**, low infant mortality and more **education for women**.

cards.front_md: In **Stage 3** of the DTM, what happens to the birth rate and why?
cards.back_md: The birth rate **falls rapidly** due to increased **birth control** and family planning, the rising **cost of raising children**, low infant mortality and more **education for women**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to the total population in **Stage 5** of the DTM?

back_blocks.md: It **slowly declines**, as the **death rate exceeds the birth rate**.

cards.front_md: What happens to the total population in **Stage 5** of the DTM?
cards.back_md: It **slowly declines**, as the **death rate exceeds the birth rate**.

front_blocks.md: Why do people have many children in **Stage 2** despite high birth rates being costly?

back_blocks.md: Children are needed as **workers**, and with **no pensions or elderly care**, people have children to look after them in old age.

cards.front_md: Why do people have many children in **Stage 2** despite high birth rates being costly?
cards.back_md: Children are needed as **workers**, and with **no pensions or elderly care**, people have children to look after them in old age.

front_blocks.md: Give two **strengths** of the demographic transition model.

back_blocks.md: It **simplifies** population change so trends are easy to identify, it can be **easily applied to different settings**, and it helps governments **plan** for predicted future changes.

cards.front_md: Give two **strengths** of the demographic transition model.
cards.back_md: It **simplifies** population change so trends are easy to identify, it can be **easily applied to different settings**, and it helps governments **plan** for predicted future changes.

back_blocks.md: What happened to the population in **Western Europe** before, during and after **industrialisation**.

cards.back_md: What happened to the population in **Western Europe** before, during and after **industrialisation**.

front_blocks.md: The DTM does not take into account migration, natural disasters, pandemics, wars or **______**, such as China's one-child policy.

back_blocks.md: The DTM does not take into account migration, natural disasters, pandemics, wars or **government policies**, such as China's one-child policy.

cards.front_md: The DTM does not take into account migration, natural disasters, pandemics, wars or **______**, such as China's one-child policy.
cards.back_md: The DTM does not take into account migration, natural disasters, pandemics, wars or **government policies**, such as China's one-child policy.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The DTM is easy to apply to LICs and MICs industrialising today.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

It is **harder** to apply to LICs and MICs today, as it is based on Western European countries that industrialised between 1800 and 1950, whereas modern countries industrialise in shorter time-frames due to globalisation.

front_blocks.md: What key assumption about development limits the DTM?

back_blocks.md: It assumes that **all countries will develop in the same way**.

cards.front_md: What key assumption about development limits the DTM?
